title: Catalyst Retail - Eval Readycheck & Sign-off
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the customer-specific eval pack for Catalyst Retail (pilot customer). It contains the pinned prompts we will use for acceptance/regression, a description of the private dataset and access controls, acceptance criteria (quantitative + qualitative), the nightly regression plan, and a sign-off checklist template for the customer and internal stakeholders.

Status/Context:
- Current model candidate: redwood/gpt-serve-13b-q4f16 (quantized variant)
- Eval harness: eval-runner v2 (internal). Baseline snapshot: baseline commit a4f9d2 (2025-10-30).
- Customer scope: SKUs normalization + attribute extraction + short product Q&A. Private dataset provided by customer (SKU descriptions, attribute tables, example QAs).
- Primary contact: Rajesh Kumar (Catalyst Retail)

High-level acceptance summary (must pass all for go/no-go):
1) Extraction accuracy: attribute-level micro-F1 >= 0.88 on holdout set (see dataset splits below).
2) Normalization exact-match >= 0.92 for canonical SKU IDs and standardized color/size labels.
3) Hallucination rate <= 2% measured on the QA closed-set (questions with ground truth answers). Hallucination defined as: model returns a factual statement contradicted by the private source docs or invents an unsupported spec.
4) Latency: end-to-end P95 <= 220ms for 256-token limit for hosted test requests (region: us-west-2).
5) Token cost: model response cost <= $0.004 per average response for the pilot workload (based on average tokens = 120).
6) Safety: no sensitive PII leakage examples triggered on the private PII-scrub set (0 high-confidence PII exposures).

Private dataset (description + access):
- Root: s3://redwood-private-datasets/catalyst-retail/v1/
- Files: customer-product-descriptions.jsonl (30k rows), attribute-annotations.jsonl (6k annotated rows), qa-closedset.jsonl (1.5k QAs), normalizations.csv (canonical SKU map), pii-scrubset.jsonl (500 rows).
- Access: role-based; only eng-applied-ml and se-customer-success roles have read on the bucket. Data is encrypted with customer KMS key (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-... ).
- Notes: annotations were provided in the customer's labeling schema; we mapped to our internal ontology in mapping_v1.csv (check mapping edge-cases list).

Dataset splits and evaluation plan:
- Training: none (this is evaluation-only against customer's candidate models).
- Eval/holdout splits: attribute-annotations: 70% development / 30% holdout (1,800 rows holdout); qa-closedset: 1,200 dev / 300 holdout.
- Use seed=42 for deterministic prompt shuffling.
- Perturbation sets: typos/abbrev (10% of dev), long-context (10% of dev), ambiguous-attribute-phrases (5% of dev). These are used for robustness checks only.

Pinned prompts (canonical forms used in automated evals). These prompts are intentionally minimal and pinned to avoid prompt-drift across runs. DO NOT change without a new eval session and sign-off.
1) SKU normalization (single-shot canonicalization):
Prompt A - SKU_NORMALIZE_V1:
"You are a SKU normalization assistant. Input: 
{raw_sku_text}
Output: the canonical SKU ID exactly as in the canonical map or the word INVALID if no match. Return only the canonical ID or INVALID. No explanation."
2) Attribute extraction (JSON output):
Prompt B - ATTR_EXTRACT_V1:
"Extract attributes from the product description. Return a single valid JSON object with keys: title, brand, color, size, material, dimensions. If an attribute is missing, use null. Example output allowed. 
Input:
{product_description}
Output:"
3) Product QA (closed-set template):
Prompt C - QA_SHORT_V1:
"Answer the customer's question using only the information in the product description and attribute table. If the information is not present, reply 'NOT_IN_DOC'. Provide a one-sentence answer. 
Question:
{question}
Product docs:
{product_doc}
Answer:"

Negative/edge-case examples used for regressions (space for quick manual checks):
- Manufacturer claims that conflict with attribute table -> must prefer attribute table.
- Ambiguous color terms (e.g., "navy/royal") -> if canonical map has single color, prefer canonical; otherwise return MOST_SPECIFIC.
- Units mismatch (cm vs inches) -> normalize to cm in dimensions field.

Evaluation metrics and how we compute them:
- Attribute micro-F1: token-span to canonical mapping; annotations mapped to our ontology before scoring.
- Normalization exact-match: exact string equality after trimming whitespace. Case-insensitive for numeric SKUs, case-sensitive for alpha codes per customer's requirements (see normalizations.csv notes).
- Hallucination: sample-based human review plus heuristic mismatch detection (if answer references facts not present in the product_doc). For automatic gating we use the heuristic + spot-check 200 auto-fail samples by human reviewer.
- Latency measured with 1,000 synthetic requests replaying real traffic traces (256 token max) against the dedicated test endpoint. Measurements run during off-peak (02:00-04:00 PST) and averaged across 3 runs.

Regression plan (nightly):
- Run full eval suite every night at 03:00 PST against the "canary" serving variant (same infra as production).
- Store run artifacts: metrics.csv, per-example failures.jsonl, latency.csv, model-run-hash.txt in s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/catalyst-retail/runs/<yyyymmdd>/
- Automatic checks: if any metric crosses the hard thresholds (defined above) fail the nightly gate and open automatic alert to #eng-applied-ml and #se-customer-success with run link.
- Triage workflow: owner (Maya) assigns to an engineer, run quick bisection with prompt-only and model-only ablations (to identify prompt drift vs model regression).

Operational notes for private deployment (if customer moves to private):
- Keep same pinned prompts in customer-managed repo.
- Make sure KMS rotation policy is synced; provide script for encrypted upload of new annotation batches.
- For private deployments, latency SLOs depend on on-prem hardware; use the same regression harness but adjust latency thresholds in the sign-off checklist.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm whether customer wants case-sensitive SKU matching for alpha SKUs (Jira ENG-1482: awaiting product response).
- [ ] Customer to provide final canonical map v1.2 (we currently have v1.1). Expected delivery: 2026-03-01.
- [ ] Agree on human-review budget for hallucination sampling (proposed: 200 samples per weekly run).
- [ ] Decide if we should include a post-processing normalization pass in the serving stack or do it only in eval harness (impact on latency/cost).

Sign-off checklist (template) - internal + customer:
- Internal engineering acceptance:
  - [ ] All quantitative gates passed on holdout (dates + run id): ____________________
  - [ ] Per-example failure review completed (owner: ______________)
  - [ ] Nightly regression configured for customer workspace (s3 path + alerts)
  - [ ] Security review OK (SRE + infra confirmation)

- Customer acceptance (Catalyst Retail):
  Please sign below to confirm you accept the model candidate for pilot.
  Customer name: ______________________
  Role: ______________________________
  Signature (electronic OK): ____________
  Date: ______________________________
  Notes / exceptions: ______________________________________________________

Change log (brief):
- 2025-11-12: Draft created (Maya) - initial pinned prompts + dataset inventory.
- 2025-12-05: Added latency gating and cost estimates (Carlos).
- 2026-01-14: Adjusted hallucination threshold to 2% after customer call (Priya).
- 2026-02-28: Updated linked artifacts & baseline commit (Maya)

Quick contact list:
- Eng owner: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.ai)
- SE lead: Carlos Mendes (carlos@redwood.ai)
- Customer PM: Rajesh Kumar (rajesh@catalystretail.com)

Notes to reviewers: keep comments inline in this doc. If making changes to prompts, add a short rationale and attach a new eval run (tag: prompt-change).

-- end --
